claims.text: Pulumi's Output<T> toString placeholder text reads `Calling [toString] on an [Output<T>] is not supported` when an output is treated as a plain value.
A page exists at /docs/iac/operations/troubleshooting/output-values/ titled 'Output value errors' that covers symptoms of treating an output as if it were already a plain value.
The Pulumi docs page at /docs/iac/operations/troubleshooting/output-values/ exists and covers errors from stringifying, branching on, or reading an output value like a plain value.
Pulumi Cloud returns the error "409 conflict: Another update is currently in progress" for update conflicts.
x86_64 binaries running under Rosetta 2 on Apple Silicon can cause crashes or hangs.
A recently deleted stack can be recovered from the Pulumi Cloud console, including after an accidental `pulumi stack rm --force`.
`pulumi` supports `--target` and `--exclude` options to limit operations to specific resources.
Running `pulumi logs share` securely sends logs from a failed operation to the Pulumi team.
The `read ".pulumi/meta.yaml"` error occurs when the CLI can't access a self-managed state backend.
Pulumi resource properties are represented as Outputs rather than plain values because their real values are not known until the providing resource has been created or updated.
Converting a Pulumi Output to a string directly (instead of via apply) does not raise an error by default; Pulumi silently substitutes a placeholder message.
In TypeScript, the string conversion of an Output contains the text `Calling [toString] on an [Output<T>] is not supported`, followed by guidance to use apply or pulumi.interpolate.
In TypeScript, calling JSON.stringify() on an Output produces a `Calling [toJSON] on an [Output<T>] is not supported` string rather than the value.
In Python, formatting an Output as a string yields text containing `Calling __str__ on an Output[T] is not supported`, and Pulumi also logs a warning.
In Python, passing an Output to json.dumps() fails with `TypeError: Object of type Output is not JSON serializable`; Output.json_dumps() is the alternative.
In Go, passing a pulumi.StringOutput where a string is expected is a compile error.
In C#, the string conversion of an Output contains `Calling [ToString] on an [Output<T>] is not supported`, followed by guidance to use Apply or Output.Format.
Setting environment variable PULUMI_ERROR_OUTPUT_STRING=true (for TypeScript, Python, and C#) makes Output-to-string conversion throw an exception instead of returning placeholder text.

String-composition helpers: pulumi.interpolate and pulumi.concat in TypeScript, Output.concat/Output.format/Output.json_dumps in Python, pulumi.Sprintf/pulumi.JSONMarshal in Go, and Output.Format in C#.
The apply callback runs asynchronously once the output resolves, generally after the program's top-level code has finished, so an outer variable assigned within it is undefined when read earlier.
Most resource inputs accept outputs as well as plain values; a resource's logical name is one position that cannot.
In dynamically typed languages an `if` on an Output is generally always true because the Output object is evaluated; in statically typed languages it is usually a compile error.
Values known at program start, such as stack configuration read with pulumi.Config, environment variables, or hardcoded flags, are plain values and can be branched on normally.
Passing an Output as a resource logical name or loop bound fails to compile in TypeScript, Go, and C#.
In Python, passing an Output as a resource's logical name raises `TypeError: Expected resource name to be a string`.
In Python, range(some_output) raises `TypeError: 'Output' object cannot be interpreted as an integer`.
In Python, using an Output as a dictionary key does not raise; it silently keys on the Output object itself.
Pulumi has no supported way to block the program and synchronously read a resolved value from an Output.
`pulumi stack output <name>` reads a single stack output after a deployment.
The Automation API exposes an `outputs` field on the result of running an update (e.g. res.Outputs in Go).
Linked pages exist: /docs/iac/concepts/inputs-outputs/apply/, /all/, /docs/iac/concepts/stacks/#stackreferences, /docs/iac/concepts/automation-api/.
